drug_class: Sympathomimetic amine / appetite suppressant (Schedule IV controlled substance)
purpose: Phentermine is used to help with weight loss in adults who are overweight or obese. It is meant to be used along with a healthy diet and regular exercise, not as a replacement for them. It is typically prescribed for short-term use, usually a few weeks to a few months.
how_it_works: Phentermine works by affecting certain chemicals in your brain that control appetite, making you feel less hungry throughout the day. Think of it as turning down the volume on your hunger signals so it is easier to eat less. It also gives you a mild boost in energy, similar to how your body responds to stress or excitement.
common_side_effects: Dry mouth, trouble sleeping (especially if taken too late in the day), feeling jittery or nervous, increased heart rate, headache, constipation, and dizziness. Some people also notice an unpleasant taste or feeling of restlessness.
warnings: Do not take phentermine if you have heart disease, high blood pressure, an overactive thyroid, glaucoma, or a history of drug abuse. It should never be taken with or within 14 days of taking MAO inhibitor antidepressants, as this can be dangerous. It can be habit-forming, so take only as prescribed. Tell your doctor if you feel your heart racing, have chest pain, or notice mood changes. Do not take it if you are pregnant or breastfeeding.
typical_dosing: The most common dose is one 37.5 mg tablet or capsule taken once a day, usually in the morning before breakfast or 1-2 hours after breakfast. A lower dose of 8 mg (Lomaira) can be taken up to three times a day, about 30 minutes before meals. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and avoid taking it late in the day to prevent sleep problems.
